Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The morphism <MATH_0002> is locally of finite presentation.
<STRUCT_0003> For every affine opens <MATH_0003>, <MATH_0004>
with <MATH_0005> the ring map
<MATH_0006> is of finite presentation.
<STRUCT_0004> There exist an open covering <MATH_0007>
and open coverings <MATH_0008> such
that each of the morphisms <MATH_0009>, <MATH_0010>
is locally of finite presentation.
<STRUCT_0005> There exist an affine open covering <MATH_0011>
and affine open coverings <MATH_0012> such
that the ring map <MATH_0013> is
of finite presentation, for all <MATH_0014>.
<STRUCT_0006>
Moreover, if <MATH_0015> is locally of finite presentation then for
any open subschemes <MATH_0016>, <MATH_0017> with <MATH_0018>
the restriction <MATH_0019> is locally of finite presentation.

This follows from Lemma <REF_0001> if we show that
the property ``<MATH_0001> is of finite presentation'' is local.
We check conditions (a), (b) and (c) of Definition
<REF_0002>.
By Algebra, Lemma <REF_0003>
being of finite presentation is stable under base change and hence
we conclude (a) holds. By Algebra, Lemma
<REF_0004> being of finite presentation
is stable under composition and trivially for any ring
<MATH_0002> the ring map <MATH_0003> is of finite presentation.
We conclude (b) holds. Finally, property (c) is true
according to Algebra, Lemma <REF_0005>.
